best_echo_sets.commentary: This set sacrifices Rebecca's personal damage in order to provide higher buffing to a single character. It provides an extra 10% Energy Regen to the wielder unconditionally and gives 22.5% ATK to the incoming character for 15s after casting Outro skill.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Provides 10% DMG Bonus for 15s as well as DMG reduction for 3 hits. If hit 3 times, the damage buff runs out, which means you want to avoid getting hit to make full use of this Echo; however, it's optimal on Rebecca without Quickswap as it can be cast right before her Ultimate (after her Forte Heavy Attack) in order to cancel the animation, buff your main DPS, the most of Rebecca's rotation, as well as the most of your Support's rotation (just frontload their damage).

Theoretically a more consistent option in quickswap, that can increase the incoming character's DMG Bonus by 12% via Outro as well as restore extra Energy for the character if its damage lands on the enemy. However, this Echo is a transform that takes time to cast during Rebecca's rotation, meaning it must be cast before her rotation - restricting this Echo's use to quickswap teams.

best_echo_sets.commentary: Grants Rebecca an easily activated Basic and Heavy DMG Bonus increase. This is a 1-piece set with only 1 Main Echo possible that also grants Rebecca additional CRIT Rate, making it the overall best blend of stats she can have for her personal damage (sacrificing team buffing in the process), paired alongside 2 2-piece sets. These sets include:

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Only Echo for the Shadow of Shattered Dreams set, simple summon Echo that grants an extra 15% CRIT Rate to Lucy or Rebecca.

best_echo_sets.commentary: Lynae's Signature Echo set can be utilized by Rebecca (in Lucy's team specifically) which can grant a higher total set of buffs than what Moonlit Clouds provides. However, due to the inability of this Echo set to increase Rebecca and her Support's damage as well (possible with Bell-Borne Geochelone main Echo), it is a very close contender but not a stronger one than Moonlit Clouds, with lower overall usability in non-Lucy teams. It is still a close contender if you have the Echoes and don't want to farm a separate Moonlit set for Rebecca though.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Simple summon Echo with the special property of giving an extra 10% DMG Bonus to the next character switched into via an Outro. Sacrifices small amounts of personal damage usually seen in Main Echoes for extra damage increase to the DPS, which is highly preferred by buff-focused characters.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Rebecca's Signature is of course her best in slot, as it can boost party-wide ATK more significantly than its permanent counterpart Static Mist, while giving Rebecca higher damaging stats with its Basic DMG and CRIT DMG bonuses.

Good for a free character, but still a free character. Don't expect her to shatter the meta; she only brings a good alternative for Heavy Attackers and is only best in slot for an average DPS.

sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Rebecca is a 5-star Electro Pistols buffer who specializes in dealing Basic Attack damage and buffing Heavy Attacks. She has access to the Hack mechanic, a variant of Tune Rupture, and provides a secondary source of damage as well as Heavy Attack-related buffs to enhance your Main DPS's firepower as much as possible.

Rebecca has 2 states she can switch between freely in order to complete her rotations: Huntress and Guts. She swaps between them on every Intro and Skill cast, starting in Huntress state. Practically, she will use Guts state to generate most of her Forte gauge, then cast her Forte Heavy Attack in Huntress state and Outro, creating a loop since every rotation starts in Huntress state, switching to Guts upon Intro, then back to Huntress via one Skill, leaving her in Huntress state for the start of every rotation.

Each state brings small self-buffs to Rebecca, being 30% CRIT DMG and 15% DEF Ignore buffs, where she activates both at once upon casting Intro thanks to her automatically replenished Forte resource, Hot Hand.

Her manually replenished resource, called Fervor, is charged via her Intro, Basic Attacks and Skill. When fully replenished, she casts a special Forte Heavy Attack, dealing a good amount of damage and restoring a lot of Concerto.

Rebecca's Ultimate restores a ton of Concerto and deals a lot of damage as well. It occurs in 3 stages where Rebecca shoots 15 bullets total, progressively getting enhanced as the Basic Attack or Ultimate button is pressed every 5 shots (indicated on her Forte gauge). She then finishes off with a big blast of additional damage and Concerto that can be Swap-cancelled in optimal rotations. It also grants a small 20% ATK buff to the team upon casting.

Finally, her Outro amplifies All-type DMG and summons a turret that progressively increases the Heavy Attack DMG of the on-field character, the turret dealing constant damage as well. This totals up to 15% General Amplification and 35% Heavy Attack DMG Amplification, giving a maximum of 50% Amplification to Heavy Attackers when the full buffs are acquired  (this is instant for Lucy, but takes the full 14s for other characters).

Additionally, similarly to Lucy, Rebecca has access to a unique Tune Break response called Hack. It functions the same as Tune Rupture, just under a different name, but uses the same scalings and general mechanics otherwise, overall enhancing the damage of your Tune Break Skill casts when applied by several of Rebecca's attacks.

As a result, Rebecca's rotation will have her progressively work up towards her Forte Heavy Attack via 3 Basic Attacks and a Skill before finally casting the Heavy, followed by her Ultimate, and swapping out of her finisher attack (provided enough Concerto has been built ahead of time).

Rebecca deals good damage and has good Heavy Attack buffing potential. Functionally, in spite of a quite lengthy rotation (over 7 seconds in all situations), she is still an alternative to the already proven meta Heavy Attack buffer, being Mortefi. As they are both free to acquire and have strong Heavy ATK buffing potential and a reliance on the same weapon and Echo set, being Static Mist and Moonlit Clouds, they fulfill the same niche. Disregarding different elements, which may give the advantage to one or the other depending on elemental resistance, Rebecca is generally slightly stronger in all Heavy Attack teams, with characters like Jiyan, Augusta and Phoebe, especially considering when her Signature Weapon is acquired. Obviously, Rebecca is also best used alongside Lucy, with whom she attains very solid performance although not meta-shaping.

In conclusion, for a free character, Rebecca is quite serviceable, being a "second Mortefi" of sorts who can strongly contribute to your Heavy Attack main damage dealers, having a particularly strong synergy with Lucy for several use cases in all Heavy Attack-based teams in the game. She is strongly recommended to build if you have a valid use case for her on one of your Heavy Attack-based teams, as she works well even without her Signature weapon or extra Sequence nodes, making her accessible and viable, particularly when paired with Lucy if you own her (although that's not necessary to have her perform well)!

synergies.commentary: yangyang-xuanling is the highest Heavy Attack damage dealer in the game. It's no surprise that Rebecca's best team is alongside her as she is her best Heavy Attack DMG buffer, on par with the generalist top tier Lynae. Finally, while Rebecca can detach from Lucy, Lucy definitely can't detach from Rebecca; both characters are capable of increasing each other's damage substantially and interact together via the Hack mechanic, making it Rebecca's second best pairing.

Rebecca can also pair successfully with a wide variety of Heavy Attack damage dealers, being akin to a second Mortefi of sorts. Thanks to her solid personal damage and ability to buff Heavy Attacks via her Outro, she fits nicely for all Heavy damage dealers listed prior as a capable buffer.

Rebecca can use a variety of generalist Supports for her team's third slot. Mornye is ideal for the team with Lucy to put the highest possible emphasis on Hack damage via her ability to buff the team's Off-Tune Buildup Rate. In other teams however (or simply in Whimpering Wastes where building off-tune multiple times on the same enemy will almost never happen), Shorekeeper may prove a stronger alternative due to her ability to buff the team's CRIT Rate and DMG, while Verina is the old reliable alternative to Shorekeeper with lower buffs but always being accessible on the permanent banner.
